property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the

    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

# Outcome sub-dossier — WashingtonFirst Bankshares, Inc. realized record after combination with Sandy Spring Bancorp, Inc., ~3-5-year horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the acquired company terminated its SEC
> registration shortly after closing, there is no subsequent stand-alone 10-K for it; the
> realized record is traced through the acquirer's consolidated filings, to the extent
> they separately identify facts tied to the acquired business. This sub-dossier contains
> no information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- WashingtonFirst Bankshares, Inc. filed a Form 15-12B, Certification and Notice of
  Termination of Registration, terminating the registration of its common stock under
  Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act. [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-18-001834, Form
  15-12B, filed 2018-01-11]
- No Form 10-K (or any other periodic report) was filed under WashingtonFirst
  Bankshares, Inc.'s own CIK (0001476264) after its final annual report, which covered
  fiscal year 2016; consequently there is no audited stand-alone financial record for the
  entity for the ~2020-2022 outcome window. [SRC: SEC EDGAR filing history, CIK
  0001476264, https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001476264&type=10-K]
- The acquired bank subsidiary was combined into the acquirer's bank at the legal-entity
  level and is not reported as a separate business segment or reporting unit in the
  acquirer's subsequent annual reports. [SRC: SEC accession 0000824410-21-000017, Sandy
  Spring Bancorp, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2020]

## Residual acquisition-accounting items tagged to the acquired entity in the acquirer's later filings
- The acquirer's fiscal-year-2020 Form 10-K reports merger-and-acquisition expense of
  $11.8 million recognized in 2018 in connection with the WashingtonFirst acquisition
  (compared with $1.3 million of merger-and-acquisition expense from a separate,
  subsequent acquisition in 2019). [SRC: SEC accession 0000824410-21-000017, Form 10-K]
- The same filing reports that, in connection with the WashingtonFirst acquisition, the
  acquirer assumed $25.0 million in subordinated debt (with a $2.2 million associated
  purchase premium); as of December 31, 2020, $20.0 million of that assumed debt
  remained classified as Tier 2 regulatory capital. [SRC: SEC accession
  0000824410-21-000017, Form 10-K]
- The same filing reports that, also in connection with the WashingtonFirst acquisition,
  the acquirer assumed $10.3 million in callable junior subordinated debt securities
  (with a $0.1 million associated purchase premium), and that during the first quarter
  of 2020 the acquirer redeemed the entire $10.3 million outstanding principal balance of
  that assumed debt. [SRC: SEC accession 0000824410-21-000017, Form 10-K]
- The same filing reports a $1.8 million tax benefit recognized in 2020 from carrying
  back, under CARES Act provisions, net operating losses that had been acquired as part
  of the 2018 WashingtonFirst acquisition (carried back to tax years 2013-2015). [SRC:
  SEC accession 0000824410-21-000017, Form 10-K]
- These are acquisition-accounting and tax/capital line items identified in the notes to
  the acquirer's consolidated financial statements; the filing does not present a
  business-performance trajectory (e.g., revenue, deposits, net income, or customer
  counts) specifically attributable to the acquired business on a standalone basis for
  this or any later period reviewed. [SRC: SEC accession 0000824410-21-000017, Form 10-K]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because WashingtonFirst Bankshares, Inc. terminated its SEC registration within
  roughly ten days of closing and was not carried forward as a separately reported
  business by the acquirer, there is no public, audited 3-5-year outcome record for the
  entity as a standalone business. The only traceable post-closing facts in the
  acquirer's later filings are residual acquisition-accounting and tax/capital items
  (merger-and-acquisition expense, assumed subordinated debt and its subsequent partial
  redemption, and a net-operating-loss tax benefit) tied to the 2018 transaction, not a
  disclosed business-performance trajectory. [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-18-001834,
  Form 15-12B; SEC accession 0000824410-21-000017, Form 10-K]

[SLICE END]
